text: Westport Albion’s transition to a direct, vertical passing strategy in a 4-4-2 formation paid dividends in controlling the final stages of the first half, as evidenced by five entries into the final third and a slight territorial dominance at 55.8% field tilt. Although they registered only one low-xG shot in that period, their ability to maintain possession with less pressing pressure compared to Kingsmoor (PPDA 11.5 vs. 6.8) allowed them to dictate the game's rhythm effectively. The saved header by Rafael Delacroix just after halftime exemplifies their use of direct aerial ball progression to create quick chances against Kingsmoor’s wide crossing play [#862]. For coaching focus, emphasize refining the timing and accuracy of vertical passes in the final third to increase shot quality and capitalize on the momentum created by structured, central attacks.
